post.description:
Search and retrieve logs across user's repositories.

Supports these modes:
- Full-text search: provide `query`; each namespace uses BM25 relevance and offset
  pagination. Canonical `order` and line cursors are rejected; deprecated
  `order_by` is ignored.
- Log reading: omit `query` and provide `job_id` or `vm_id`; results use cursor
  pagination ordered by `line_number.asc` (default) or `line_number.desc`.
  Replay `next_cursor` as `cursor` with the same `order`.
- Resume tokens: set logs_protocol=2 for job reads. Pass next_resume_token
  back as resume_token with the same order and filters. The token remembers
  the execution, log source, and last line confirmed in storage. GitHub
  fallback continues to use next_cursor/cursor. Older clients omit logs_protocol.
- Repository reads: omit `query`, execution IDs, and cursors; results use
  timestamp order within each namespace and bounded offset pagination.
  Results are concatenated in repository order and, within each repository,
  in month order, preserving each query's row order without a global sort.
  This also applies to full-text searches. No line order or cursor is returned
  for repository reads.
- Searches read monthly namespaces. Missing namespaces are empty; backend failures return
  503. Full-text search and repository reads cap offset plus limit at 10000.

Repository filtering:
- `organization_id`: Search repositories in one Avrea organization
- `repository_ids`: Search specific repositories by Avrea ID (rep-xxx format)
- No organization or repository filter: Search all repositories the user can access

A `vm_id` without `job_id` must include `repository_ids` so authorization
does not expand to the user's full cross-organization repository set.

Results are filtered to only include logs from repositories the user has access to.

get.description:
List repositories in an organization that the user can access.

Cursor-paginated by ``(repository_full_name, repository_id)`` ascending —
the same shape as ``/orgs/{org}/workflow-runs`` and ``/orgs/{org}/jobs``.
Pass the previous response's ``pagination.next_cursor`` verbatim to fetch
the next page; ``None`` when no more rows. ``q`` and ``repository_ids``
narrow the listing (typeahead search and by-id resolution); both compose
with the cursor because they don't change the order. Identity-bound
complete permission baselines are refreshed in the background, with stale
serving bounded to 48 hours.

get.description:
Resolve a repository full_name to its Avrea repository_id within an organization.

Returns 404 if the repository is not found in the org or the caller lacks access.
The 404 body for true misses (repo not in org) embeds ``nearby_full_names`` +
``other_orgs`` so clients can render a "did you mean?" hint without a second
round-trip. The 404 for unsupported-platform / no-access is a bare
``message`` so we don't leak existence.

get.description:
Resolve a GitHub workflow run id (the integer in ``actions/runs/<id>``)
to the Avrea ``run-xxx`` record in one round-trip.

Saves callers the dance of ``GET /workflow-runs?platform_run_id=...``
+ unwrapping ``data[0]`` (which silently returns nothing when the run
isn't visible). 404 when no matching run exists or the caller lacks
access — same existence-hiding shape as the by-id endpoint.

When a workflow is rerun, GitHub keeps the same ``platform_run_id``
but increments ``platform_run_attempt``. This endpoint resolves to
the **latest attempt** (highest ``platform_run_attempt``).

Cancel an in-progress or queued workflow run.

Supports GitHub Actions and Avrea CI. Returns `status="already_terminal"`
(HTTP 200) when the run has finished. GitHub source repositories require
source write access; native runs on other sources require organization
admin access. Scoped tokens cannot cancel runs.
